reviews.review:
play me1 and me2 first and then transfer your me2 save to me3, it's essential for playing the franchise properly. me3 is fantastic but there's a few things to note about the steam release, mainly that it also requires origin to be installed (like most ea games nowadays unfortunately).

another VERY important thing is that the game might not launch. this can be fixed by going to this file [b]%PROGRAMDATA%\Electronic Arts\EA Services\License[/b] and deleting all files in it.

a lot of people were unhappy about the ending, so you might want to download the extended cut dlc to remedy that. still, this franchise is really worth playing.

PSA: This came out in 2012. The reason why the game is still 30 dollars, is because that's half of 60, a full-price mainstream AAA game on day 1 of release, like DOOM Eternal. Their business strategy is to cut the game in half and sell both halves at a painstakingly-enduring 30 dollars each in order to keep the cost of this game stable, because this game is not complete without the DLC. If you only buy the first half of the game, the base game, playing will feel like wandering through an empty wasteland and you'll probably be finished with it in under a week. So in 20 years when the last person buys this game, they'll still have to shell out day 1 money. 

I would recommend to buy it on sale because it requires life support from EA's actually broken "lite origin launcher," and that support line was cut a long time ago... And it requires that you have an internet connection, or else you WILL NOT be able to even launch the game... and the launcher will sometimes NEVER WORK ON YOUR COMPUTER, and if you're just one of the unlucky schmucks who the game doesn't work for, "EA's customer support" (which is an oxy-moron) hung up the phone on all of us on the day it was founded...

But because of this sleazy, transparent marketing move, you can bet it's not gonna go on sale very often, and even if it does, money's that the DLC isn't going to be marked down. There's science behind that, it grabs your attention first and then causes you to think you'll miss out on this great opportunity and makes you not want to hesitate, when really you're being sucker-punched. So in short, these guys have effectively locked off all possible ways for the customer to win. That should tell you what kind of company they are.

Did I mention that certain romances are also locked behind DLC walls?
Im in the middle of some calibrations -Garrus
